title: Cell size: a driveway dip and a rear yard
process: the depth of water beside a house at 0.5, 1, 2 and 4 m cells and in the 4 m and 8 m subgrid modes
executor: node (CPU surface solver) and browser (GPU); raw measurements in street/raw/, scored by run.mjs
equations: still water: the level a volume stands at over the terrain, sum max(0, eta - z) A = V
driveway: V = P x the whole scene (everything drains to the dip); in the dip alone V = w d^2 / (2 S)
rear yard: with its 1 m passage open the yard drains to the street, depth 0 at rest; with the passage closed it holds its own rain
a coarser grid's bed is the mean of the open 1 m ground in each cell; a cell more than half building is a wall
boundaryConditions: closed on all sides; roof rain lands on the cells beside the building (the app default)
geometry: driveway: 16 x 16 m, a house row across the north half, the lot falling at 2 % from both sides to a 1 m driveway that dips at 15 % for 6 m to the garage door (0.9 m below the lot). rear yard: 16 x 16 m, a house row cut by a 1 m passage at x 7-8 m, the yard behind falling at 1 % to the passage, the street in front 0.3 m lower. Both defined at 0.5 m; the 1 m ground is its mean.

cases.unit: rain mm/h and min; times s; grid: native 0.5 m, F m cells from the 1 m ground, subgrid = the speed / screening mode

solver: FloodSim surface solver with the app's settings (hdry 1e-5 m, hfront 1e-3 m, dtDry 2 s; MUSCL minmod, HLLC, SSP-RK2, CFL 0.48). cpu rows: src/solver-cpu.js (fp64). gpu rows: src/solver-gpu.js in Chrome WebGPU (fp32). 2 m and 4 m: the app's coarsening (src/terrain.js coarsen) and its downscaling to 1 m (src/downscale.js). 4s, 8s: the subgrid mode (src/subgrid.js; GPU only).

reference.independence: the true answer comes from the 0.5 m ground and the rain depth; each grid's own answer from its block-mean ground, built here and not by the app
reference.crossCheck: refs.test.mjs: level for a volume two ways; the block mean and its wall rule

outputs: depth beside the house at the end: the deepest open cell within 2 m of the wall
for each grid: against the true depth (the 0.5 m ground's level less the 1 m ground), on the solver's own cells and on the 1 m map the app would draw
for each grid where it is plain arithmetic: against that grid's own answer (the driveway at every plain grid; the rear yard at 2 m, where the passage closes)
reported: whether the house crosses the 10 cm exposure threshold
criteriaNotes: A grid passes if the depth beside the house is within 2 cm or 10 % of the true depth. Against its own arithmetic the solver is held to 1 cm. The scene is made so the passage sits across a 2 m cell boundary; a passage that lines up with the grid would stay open. The yard storm (40 mm) was chosen before any run so that a yard holding its own rain stands above the 10 cm exposure threshold.
assumptions: no infiltration; roofs drain to the ground beside them
limitations: two made-up lots; one passage position
the peak is reported, not scored: it has no hand answer
validRange: features one cell wide at 1 m
scoring: automated: street/score.mjs builds rows with lib/score.mjs row(); one row set per executor (cpu, gpu), never merged; a case with no raw file is listed as not run and has no rows

criteriaRevisions.why: first registration, before any sandbox case was run
